claim: Aurora B kinase localizes to specific cellular locations including the inner centromere and the anaphase spindle midzone.
source: Aurora B, a component of the chromosomal passenger complex (CPC), is an essential kinase that is highly enriched at different intracellular locations from which it regulates cell division: it localizes initially at the inner centromere and subsequently at the anaphase spindle midzone (Carmena et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Carmena et al., 2012

claim: Aurora B is capable of phosphorylating substrates located at a significant distance from its major binding sites.
source: Accumulating evidence indicates that Aurora B is capable of phosphorylating substrates that are located at a significant distance from its major binding sites.
evidence: Supported by references to published work and data presented in the manuscript

claim: In anaphase, a long-range phosphorylation gradient is established around the spindle midzone that extends well beyond major sites of kinase localization.
source: In anaphase, a long-range phosphorylation gradient is established around the spindle midzone (Fuller et al., 2008; Tan and Kapoor, 2011), but extending well beyond major sites of kinase localization (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by citations and Figure 1A showing the gradient

claim: The anaphase phosphorylation gradient controls the stability and length of the central spindle.
source: This phosphorylation gradient controls the stability and length of the central spindle (Ferreira et al., 2013; Uehara et al., 2013), chromosome decondensation and nuclear envelope reassembly (Afonso et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to published work

claim: The anaphase phosphorylation gradient controls chromosome decondensation and nuclear envelope reassembly.
source: This phosphorylation gradient controls the stability and length of the central spindle (Ferreira et al., 2013; Uehara et al., 2013), chromosome decondensation and nuclear envelope reassembly (Afonso et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Afonso et al., 2014

claim: During metaphase, Aurora B primary targets such as Hec1/Ndc80 are located hundreds of nanometers away at the outer kinetochore.
source: During metaphase the primary targets for Aurora B, such as the microtubule-binding protein Hec1/Ndc80, are located hundreds of nanometers away at the outer kinetochore.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of kinetochore structure

claim: Phosphorylation is lower on substrates positioned farther from Aurora B binding sites, indicating existence of a gradient of Aurora B activity.
source: As in anaphase, phosphorylation is lower on substrates positioned farther from Aurora B binding sites, indicating existence of a gradient of Aurora B activity (Keating et al., 2009; Liu et al., 2009; Welburn et al., 2010; DeLuca et al., 2011; Suzuki et al., 2014).

claim: Changes of position of as little as 30–50 nm are associated with different levels of phosphorylation of both endogenous and exogenous Aurora B substrates at kinetochores.
source: Interestingly, changes of position of as little as 30–50 nm are associated with different levels of phosphorylation of both endogenous and exogenous Aurora B substrates at kinetochores (Welburn et al., 2010; Suzuki et al., 2014), indicating that the spatial regulation of Aurora B activity is very precise.
evidence: Supported by citations to Welburn et al., 2010 and Suzuki et al., 2014

claim: The spatial regulation of Aurora B activity is very precise.
source: Interestingly, changes of position of as little as 30–50 nm are associated with different levels of phosphorylation of both endogenous and exogenous Aurora B substrates at kinetochores (Welburn et al., 2010; Suzuki et al., 2014), indicating that the spatial regulation of Aurora B activity is very precise.
evidence: Inferred from the observation of phosphorylation changes at small spatial scales

claim: Concentrating Aurora B at centromeres leads to phosphorylation of distant chromatin substrates.
source: Addition of rapamycin led to INbox recruitment to centromeres within minutes, accompanied by sensor phosphorylation; importantly the signal was visible all over the chromatin (Figure 1B).
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally using rapamycin-induced recruitment system and FRET sensor

claim: When endogenous INCENP is replaced with INbox, which is freely diffusing in the cytosol, phosphorylation is uniformly low.
source: When endogenous INCENP is replaced with INbox, which is freely diffusing in the cytosol, phosphorylation is uniformly low, indicating that the cytosolic kinase pool on its own is incapable of maintaining high kinase activity along chromosome arms.
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally in the rapamycin recruitment system

claim: The cytosolic kinase pool on its own is incapable of maintaining high kinase activity along chromosome arms.
source: When endogenous INCENP is replaced with INbox, which is freely diffusing in the cytosol, phosphorylation is uniformly low, indicating that the cytosolic kinase pool on its own is incapable of maintaining high kinase activity along chromosome arms.
evidence: Inferred from experimental observation of low phosphorylation with diffuse INbox

claim: Concentrating Aurora B at centromeres of a mammalian cell is necessary and sufficient to regulate kinase activity at distal cellular locations.
source: Thus, concentrating Aurora B at centromeres of a mammalian cell is necessary and sufficient to regulate kinase activity at distal cellular locations, warranting further investigation of the kinetic mechanisms of Aurora B autoactivation.
evidence: Concluded from the rapamycin recruitment experiments

claim: Aurora B can activate itself via phosphorylation of its activation loop and of a conserved TSS motif in the C-terminus of INCENP.
source: Most importantly, Aurora B can activate itself via phosphorylation of its activation loop and of a conserved TSS motif in the C-terminus of INCENP (Bishop and Schumacher, 2002; Honda et al., 2003; Yasui et al., 2004; Sessa et al., 2005; Kelly et al., 2007; Xu et al., 2010).

claim: Phosphatase can inactivate Aurora B kinase by dephosphorylating sites on Aurora B and INCENP.
source: Conversely, phosphatase can inactivate the kinase by dephosphorylating sites on Aurora B and INCENP (Sessa et al., 2005; Kelly et al., 2007; Rosasco-Nitcher et al., 2008), which could potentially help to shape the spatial gradient of Aurora B activity.

claim: The INCENP TSS motif is an established autophosphorylation site associated with kinase activation.
source: With purified kinase, the INCENP TSS motif, an established autophosphorylation site associated with kinase activation (Bishop and Schumacher, 2002; Honda et al., 2003; Sessa et al., 2005), was phosphorylated, as determined by immunoblotting with a phospho-specific antibody (Salimian et al., 2011; Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by citations and experimental data

claim: Phosphorylated Aurora B kinase has KM = 320 μM and kcat = 19 s-1 for chemosensor substrate.
source: Michaelis–Menten, Lineweaver–Burk and Hanes–Woolf plots were analyzed (see Materials and methods), giving KM = 320 μM and kcat = 19 s-1, similar to a previous report for Aurora A kinase (Gonzáles-Vera et al., 2009).

claim: Dephosphorylated Aurora B kinase is two orders of magnitude less active than phosphorylated Aurora B.
source: The dephosphorylated Aurora B kinase was two orders of magnitude less active than the phosphorylated Aurora B, consistent with previous studies (Eyers et al., 2005; Sessa et al., 2005), so we refer to this kinase state as partially active.
evidence: Determined experimentally and consistent with citations

claim: At 10–30 nM of partially active kinase, chemosensor phosphorylation was barely detected.
source: At 10–30 nM of partially active kinase, chemosensor phosphorylation was barely detected.

claim: At 0.16–1.5 µM kinase, chemosensor phosphorylation increased nonlinearly with time, indicating autoactivation.
source: At 0.16–1.5 µM kinase, chemosensor phosphorylation increased nonlinearly with time, indicating autoactivation (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 2G).

claim: The measured slope of autoactivation at low kinase concentrations was 1.23 ± 0.02, implying that partially active Aurora B can activate itself in cis.
source: The measured slope in our experiments with low kinase concentrations was 1.23 ± 0.02 (Figure 2C), implying that the partially active Aurora B can activate itself in cis, i.e. intramolecularly (Figure 2B).
evidence: Experimental measurement and inference from the slope value

claim: Aurora B kinase autoactivation has both cis and trans components.
source: With a computational model combining both reactions (Figure 2E), we generated a global fit to experimental curves in Figure 2A,D and determined molecular constants for the two-component autoactivation mechanism for Aurora B kinase (Table 2, Materials and methods).
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental data fitting with computational model

claim: Kinase autoactivation in cis dominates over trans-activation during initial activation at low kinase concentration.
source: This model demonstrates that kinase autoactivation in cis dominates over the trans-activation during initial activation at low kinase concentration (Figure 2—figure supplement 2, panels H and I).

claim: At high Aurora B kinase concentration, three steady-state solutions can coexist in a coupled kinase-phosphatase system.
source: Solving the differential equations describing this system in silico (see Materials and methods) reveals that at high kinase concentration three steady-state solutions could coexist (Figure 3B).

claim: Bistability arises when Aurora B kinase concentration exceeds 4 μM.
source: Bistability arises when Aurora B kinase concentration exceeds 4 μM, and further increasing Aurora B concentration broadens the range of permissible phosphatase concentrations.

claim: In the bistable region, a homogeneous mixture of kinase and phosphatase can exist in one of two stable states with different kinase activity depending on initial conditions.
source: In this region, a homogeneous mixture of kinase and phosphatase can exist in one of two stable states with different kinase activity, high or low, depending on initial conditions (Figure 3C).

claim: The coupled Aurora B kinase-phosphatase system exhibits hysteresis in the region of bistability.
source: The model also predicts hysteresis in the region of bistability. Hysteresis becomes evident at intermediate levels of phosphatase concentration (e.g. 0.4 μM in Figure 3F), when almost the entire kinase pool can be either phosphorylated (high kinase activity state) or dephosphorylated (low kinase activity state) depending on the prior state of this reaction mixture.

claim: Non-linear regimes of the Aurora B-phosphatase system are determined mostly by the parameters of the two component Aurora B autoactivation mechanism, but not by the enzymatic constants of the protein phosphatase.
source: Importantly, we find that these non-linear regimes are determined mostly by the parameters of the two component Aurora B autoactivation mechanism, but not by the enzymatic constants of the protein phosphatase (Figure 3—figure supplement 1; see Materials and methods).
evidence: Demonstrated through computational modeling with varying parameters

claim: Aurora B kinase coupled with an inactivating phosphatase exhibits robust hysteresis and bistability.
source: Thus, Aurora B kinase, coupled with an inactivating phosphatase, is predicted to exhibit robust hysteresis and bistability.

claim: The reconstituted in vitro Aurora B kinase-phosphatase system exhibits bistability and hysteresis in quantitative agreement with theoretical predictions.
source: These data, plotted as a function of phosphatase concentration in Figure 4C, define the bistable region for the homogeneous system in vitro, in quantitative agreement with model predictions.
evidence: Demonstrated through in vitro experiments matching computational predictions

claim: At intermediate phosphatase concentration (0.45 µM), kinase that was initially active robustly retained its high state, while activity remained low for kinase that was initially in the low state.
source: At 0.45 µM phosphatase, the kinase that was initially active robustly retained its high state (red data points, Figure 4B, middle graph), while the activity remained low for the kinase that was initially in the low state (blue data points, Figure 4B middle graph).

claim: The endogenous Aurora B–phosphatase system in mitotic cells exhibits bistability.
source: Analysis of a population of cells expressing the centromere-targeted sensor shows that the distribution of phosphorylation states is clearly bimodal, with distinct high and low FRET states (Figure 5A).
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally using FRET sensor in cells

claim: For intermediate concentrations of Aurora B inhibitor, both high and low phosphorylation peaks are observed in the same cell population.
source: Importantly, for some intermediate concentrations of Aurora B inhibitor, both peaks are observed in the same cell population, likely because individual cells differ slightly in their parameters, for example in membrane permeability to kinase inhibitor.
evidence: Experimental observation from FRET sensor experiments

claim: The prior history of Aurora B kinase activation affects the level of Aurora B activity in mitotic cells.
source: When the inhibitor concentration was switched to the intermediate level, however, kinase activity remained in the initial state in these mitotic cells: high if the initial condition was low inhibitor (0 to 0.6 µM) and low activity if the initial condition was high inhibitor (1.5 to 0.6 µM) (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally showing hysteresis in cells

claim: Cellular localizations of Aurora B and PP1γ phosphatase are not affected by treatment with Aurora B inhibitor ZM447439.
source: In addition, we found that cellular localizations of Aurora B and PP1γ phosphatase were not affected by treatment with this inhibitor (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), consistent with a previous report for Aurora B localization (Ditchfield et al., 2003).

claim: Bistability and hysteresis of Aurora B phosphorylation in mitotic cells are driven by the intrinsic properties of Aurora B kinase coupled with the inactivating phosphatase(s).
source: Together, these results strongly indicate that bistability and hysteresis of Aurora B phosphorylation in mitotic cells are driven by the intrinsic properties of Aurora B kinase coupled with the inactivating phosphatase(s).
evidence: Concluded from experimental observations in cells

claim: Peak Aurora B concentration at the centromere is estimated at 10 µM, dropping down to 1.5 µM along chromosome arms and 1–2 µM in the kinetochore area.
source: Peak Aurora B concentration at the centromere is estimated at 10 µM, dropping down to 1.5 µM along chromosome arms and 1–2 µM in the kinetochore area (Figure 6A).
evidence: Estimated from fluorescence intensity profiles and published data

claim: The steady-state fractions of bound and diffusing soluble Aurora B kinase pools are 75% and 25%, respectively.
source: In the model soluble kinase molecules bind and unbind these sites dynamically to achieve the steady-state fractions of the bound and diffusing soluble kinase pools of 75% and 25%, respectively (Mahen et al., 2014).

claim: The spatial model with bistability can reproduce Aurora B hysteresis observed in mitotic cells.
source: The enzymatic constant for phosphatase acting on Aurora B kinase in cells is not known, but KPM = 0.16 µM provided an excellent match with experimental measurements in cells (Figure 6C). Thus, Aurora B hysteresis in mitotic cells can be reproduced using the molecular and biochemical features which form the basis for our model and reasonable values of model parameters.
evidence: Demonstrated through computational modeling matching experimental data

claim: Bistability of the underlying biochemical pathways is required to explain hysteresis detected with the Aurora B phosphorylation sensor in cells.
source: Thus, bistability of the underlying biochemical pathways is required to explain hysteresis that we detected with the Aurora B phosphorylation sensor in cells.
evidence: Concluded from comparison of models with and without bistability

claim: Aurora B phosphorylation along chromatin propagates as a trigger wave at constant speed.
source: Indeed, the predicted plot for the timing of Aurora B activation as a function of distance from the centromere was linear, implying a constant rate of spreading (Figure 7C). To test this model prediction we plotted the time of phosphorylation as a function of distance from centromeres for the chromatin bound FRET sensor, from experiments in which ZM447439 was washed out. This dependency was also linear, strongly suggesting that phosphorylation along chromatin propagates as a trigger wave (Figure 7C).
evidence: Demonstrated through experimental measurements matching model predictions

claim: Almost the entire centromere-bound pool of prometaphase Aurora B kinase is predicted to be active, with the fraction of active kinase decreasing slightly at the kinetochore.
source: Almost the entire centromere-bound pool of prometaphase Aurora B kinase is predicted to be active, with the fraction of active kinase decreasing slightly at the kinetochore (bounded by CENP-A and Ndc80) (Figure 8A).

claim: In stretched metaphase chromatin, a region of bistability emerges at the kinetochore, hundreds of nm away from the centroid.
source: In stretched chromatin the distance between Aurora B binding sites increased correspondingly, as indicated with the white mesh in Figure 8. As a result, the local concentration of chromatin-bound kinase decreased, and a region of bistability emerged at the kinetochore, hundreds of nm away from the centroid (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).

claim: Bistable kinase-phosphatase system creates a stable and steep gradient of Aurora B kinase activity in the chromatin meshwork.
source: As we have shown earlier, the bistable kinase-phosphatase system exhibits a highly nonlinear behavior. In the chromatin meshwork, these threshold-dependent reactions created a stable and steep gradient of Aurora B kinase activity.

claim: In the model with no bistability, stretching induced a much more gradual gradient of Aurora B activity.
source: In contrast, in the model with no bistability, stretching induced a much more gradual gradient of Aurora B activity, reflecting a gradual decrease in density of centromere-bound Aurora B kinase (Figure 8B,D).

claim: Concentrating Aurora B at centromeres is necessary and sufficient for phosphorylation of distant cellular locations in mammalian cells.
source: Thus, concentrating Aurora B at centromeres of a mammalian cell is necessary and sufficient to regulate kinase activity at distal cellular locations, warranting further investigation of the kinetic mechanisms of Aurora B autoactivation.

claim: Bistability of an Aurora B-phosphatase system underlies formation of spatial phosphorylation patterns.
source: We propose that bistability of an Aurora B-phosphatase system underlies formation of spatial phosphorylation patterns, which are generated and spread from sites of kinase autoactivation, thereby regulating cell division.
evidence: Proposed based on combined experimental and modeling results

claim: Cytosolic Aurora B concentration is approximately 8.6 nM.
source: To quantify the spatial distribution of Aurora B kinase binding sites on chromatin, we used the reported soluble Aurora B concentration in cells Csol = 8.6 nM (Mahen et al., 2014)

claim: About 75% of total cellular Aurora B is in the bound form.
source: About 75% of total cellular Aurora B is in the bound form (Mahen et al., 2014)

claim: The average concentration of bound Aurora B is 6.4 µM.
source: Therefore, Cbound = 6.4 µM, leading to quantitative profiles in Figure 6—figure supplement 1 panels B and C with a peak Aurora B concentration 10 µM.
evidence: Calculated from published data and cell volume estimates

claim: The dissociation constant KD for the CPC complex is 4.8 nM.
source: Using KD = 4.8 nM for the CPC complex (Mahen et al., 2014)

claim: CPC turnover time is 50 seconds.
source: Dissociation constant koff = 0.014 s-1 for Aurora B was based on the previously measured CPC turnover time of 50 s (Murata-Hori and Wang, 2002).

claim: The Stokes radius of the CPC complex is 10 nm.
source: The diffusion coefficient for Aurora B was chosen based on the known Stokes radius of the CPC complex, 10 nm (Cormier et al., 2013)

claim: The diffusion coefficient for Aurora B is 1 µm²/s.
source: The diffusion coefficient for Aurora B was chosen based on the known Stokes radius of the CPC complex, 10 nm (Cormier et al., 2013), which corresponds to D = 1 µm2/s (Luby-Phelps, 2000).
evidence: Calculated from Stokes radius using published relationship

claim: Interkinetochore distance increases approximately 2-fold from prometaphase to metaphase in HeLa cells.
source: This corresponds to interkinetochore distances 1.4 µm and 0.8 µm in metaphase and prometaphase, respectively, as in HeLa cells (Wan et al., 2009).

claim: Bistability affords versatile control of the position and steepness of Aurora B activity gradients.
source: Thus, bistability affords versatile control of the position and steepness of the resulting gradient, which is thought to be essential for regulation of kinetochore-microtubule interactions (Funabiki and Wynne, 2013; Krenn and Musacchio, 2015).
evidence: Concluded from modeling results and supported by citations about functional importance

claim: Bistability is likely to play an important role in establishing a gradient of Aurora B activity around the spindle midzone in anaphase.
source: Bistability is also likely to play an important role in establishing a gradient of Aurora B activity around the spindle midzone in anaphase, though the mechanistic details may be different and need to be examined separately.
evidence: Speculated based on findings in other contexts

claim: Other mechanisms may also regulate spatial patterns of Aurora B activity, such as changes in Aurora B enrichment at centromeres as chromosomes align.
source: In addition to the bistable system described here, other mechanisms may also regulate spatial patterns of Aurora B activity, such as changes in Aurora B enrichment at centromeres as chromosomes align (Salimian et al., 2011)
evidence: Acknowledged as additional mechanism supported by citation

claim: Localized phosphatase activity at different cellular locations may regulate spatial patterns of Aurora B activity.
source: In addition to the bistable system described here, other mechanisms may also regulate spatial patterns of Aurora B activity, such as changes in Aurora B enrichment at centromeres as chromosomes align (Salimian et al., 2011) and localized phosphatase activity at different cellular locations, such as kinetochores or centromeres or on chromatin (Trinkle-Mulcahy et al., 2003; 2006; Kitajima et al., 2006; Riedel et al., 2006; Tang et al., 2006; Liu et al., 2010; Foley et al., 2011).
evidence: Acknowledged as additional mechanism supported by citations

claim: Localization of both PP1 and PP2A at kinetochores depends on microtubule attachment and tension.
source: Localization of both PP1 and PP2A at kinetochores depends on microtubule attachment and tension, and changes in these local phosphatase activities may modulate the location of the bistable region of Aurora B activity or exert direct effects on substrates located in the immediate vicinity.
evidence: Based on established knowledge in the field

claim: HeLa cells were purchased from ATCC.
source: HeLa cells were purchased from ATCC and identity was not further authenticated.

claim: Cells were shown to be free of Mycoplasma contamination by DNA staining.
source: Cells were shown to be free of Mycoplasma contamination by DNA staining.

claim: A HeLa cell line expressing GFP-Aurora B has low expression level compared to endogenous Aurora B.
source: A HeLa cell line expressing GFP-Aurora B was generated as described previously (Salimian et al., 2011), and the expression level of GFP-Aurora B was shown by immunoblotting to be low compared to endogenous Aurora B.

claim: The INbox fragment is sufficient for Aurora B kinase autoactivation.
source: To determine the kinetic constants for Aurora B autoactivation, we measured phosphorylation in vitro in real time using purified recombinant Aurora B kinase with an INbox fragment, which is sufficient for kinase autoactivation (Sessa et al., 2005; Rosasco-Nitcher et al., 2008)

claim: Lambda phage phosphatase dephosphorylates INCENP.
source: To examine activity of Aurora B in the dephosphorylated state, we incubated the kinase with λ phage phosphatase, which has previously been reported to dephosphorylate INCENP (Rosasco-Nitcher et al., 2008), and observed loss of INCENP phosphorylation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).

claim: Phosphonoacetic acid inhibits lambda phage phosphatase.
source: Phosphonoacetic acid was then added to inhibit the phosphatase (Reiter et al., 2002)

claim: The cytosolic Aurora B concentration range of 10-30 nM was reported for cells.
source: This finding is consistent with our results using INbox replacement in cells with no rapamycin, since this low concentration range was reported for cytosolic Aurora B (Mahen et al., 2014).

claim: Previous studies have reported that Aurora B autoactivation takes place in trans.
source: Previous studies have reported that this autoactivation takes place in trans (Sessa et al., 2005; Rosasco-Nitcher et al., 2008)

claim: Trans autoactivation predicts that the coefficient for chemosensor phosphorylation increase vs. kinase concentration is close to 2 when plotted on a logarithmic scale.
source: Previous studies have reported that this autoactivation takes place in trans (Sessa et al., 2005; Rosasco-Nitcher et al., 2008) (Figure 2B), predicting that the coefficient for this increase vs. kinase concentration is close to 2 when plotted on a logarithmic scale.
evidence: Theoretical prediction based on trans mechanism

claim: Only the active, already phosphorylated Aurora B kinase can activate in trans.
source: We confirm these initial findings, but we also find that only the active, already phosphorylated Aurora B kinase can activate in trans.

claim: The cis step of Aurora B autoactivation may reflect autophosphorylation of the activation loop.
source: The cis step may reflect autophosphorylation of the activation loop, as shown for Aurora A (Dodson et al., 2013), while the TSS motif of INCENP is phosphorylated in trans.
evidence: Speculated based on analogy to Aurora A and supported by citation

claim: The rate of the in cis reaction has a large impact on the bistable region of the Aurora B-phosphatase system.
source: The significance of the in cis reaction is not fully understood, but we show that its rate has a large impact on the bistable region of the Aurora B-phosphatase system, as discussed below.

claim: This is the first reconstitution of bistability and hysteresis in vitro for any kinase-phosphatase pair.
source: Importantly, we were able to observe this non-trivial behavior in vitro using purified Aurora B kinase and λ phosphatase, which to the best of our knowledge is the first reconstitution of this kind for any kinase-phosphatase pair.

claim: Bistability depends strongly on the Aurora B kinase autoactivation mechanism.
source: Importantly, our theoretical analyses predicted that bistability depends strongly on the Aurora B kinase autoactivation mechanism, while kinetic constants for the dephosphorylation reaction have much less impact (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).

claim: Kinetic constants for the dephosphorylation reaction have much less impact on bistability than autoactivation parameters.
source: Importantly, our theoretical analyses predicted that bistability depends strongly on the Aurora B kinase autoactivation mechanism, while kinetic constants for the dephosphorylation reaction have much less impact (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).

claim: The simplified reconstitution in vitro using non-physiological λ phosphatase can still exhibit nonlinear regimes that exist in physiological cell context.
source: Thus, although our simplified reconstitution in vitro used the non-physiological λ phosphatase, the model suggested that these nonlinear regimes could exist in a physiological cell context, where Aurora B kinase is coupled with its native phosphatase partner(s).
evidence: Inferred from modeling showing independence from specific phosphatase parameters

claim: The distinct phosphorylation states in mitotic cells arise from threshold-dependent autoactivation of the highly concentrated pool of centromere-localized Aurora B.
source: We therefore explain the distinct phosphorylation states in mitotic cells as arising from the threshold-dependent autoactivation of the highly concentrated pool of centromere-localized Aurora B, propagated at long distance via the chromatin-bound and cytosolic pools of Aurora B.
evidence: Proposed mechanism based on combined experimental and modeling results

claim: The consistency between findings in vitro and in vivo indicates that key features of the Aurora B-phosphatase system that underlie cellular behaviors have been captured.
source: The consistency between our findings in vitro and in vivo indicates that we have captured key features of the Aurora B-phosphatase system that underlie cellular behaviors.
evidence: Concluded from agreement between in vitro and in vivo results

claim: Long-range propagation of Aurora B phosphorylation has been observed previously.
source: Long-range propagation of Aurora B phosphorylation has been observed previously (Wang et al., 2011), but it was thought to be caused by simple diffusion of activated Aurora B released from the sites of concentration.

claim: Trigger waves propagate at constant speed.
source: We quantified these waves and found that they propagate at constant speed (Figure 7), strongly implying that they are sustained by a more complex reaction-diffusion mechanism in a bistable system.

claim: A model lacking bistability in the range of physiological Aurora B concentrations fails to reproduce trigger waves and other results in cells.
source: Additionally, we demonstrate that a highly similar reaction-diffusion model, which also includes kinase autoactivation coupled with inactivating phosphatase but lacks bistability in the range of physiological Aurora B concentrations, fails to reproduce the trigger waves and other results in cells.

claim: Different non-linear mechanisms operating in excitable media play important roles in developmental biology and cell division.
source: Different non-linear mechanisms operating in excitable media have been shown to play important roles in developmental biology and cell division (Turing, 1952; Caudron et al., 2005; Maini et al., 2006; Karsenti, 2008; Chang and Ferrell, 2013)

claim: Non-linear mechanisms play important roles in the cardiovascular system and blood clotting.
source: Different non-linear mechanisms operating in excitable media have been shown to play important roles in developmental biology and cell division (Turing, 1952; Caudron et al., 2005; Maini et al., 2006; Karsenti, 2008; Chang and Ferrell, 2013), the cardiovascular system and blood clotting (Lobanova and Ataullakhanov, 2003; Sharma et al., 2009)

claim: Non-linear mechanisms play important roles in kinase signaling.
source: Different non-linear mechanisms operating in excitable media have been shown to play important roles in developmental biology and cell division (Turing, 1952; Caudron et al., 2005; Maini et al., 2006; Karsenti, 2008; Chang and Ferrell, 2013), the cardiovascular system and blood clotting (Lobanova and Ataullakhanov, 2003; Sharma et al., 2009), kinase signaling (Kholodenko, 2009)

claim: Non-linear mechanisms play important roles in intracellular patterning and size control.
source: Different non-linear mechanisms operating in excitable media have been shown to play important roles in developmental biology and cell division (Turing, 1952; Caudron et al., 2005; Maini et al., 2006; Karsenti, 2008; Chang and Ferrell, 2013), the cardiovascular system and blood clotting (Lobanova and Ataullakhanov, 2003; Sharma et al., 2009), kinase signaling (Kholodenko, 2009) and intracellular patterning and size control (Meyers et al., 2006; Fischer-Friedrich et al., 2010; Hachet et al., 2011; Subramanian et al., 2015).

claim: Centromeric chromatin is a mechanical medium capable of sustaining biochemical reactions via a spatially non-uniform distribution of Aurora B kinase.
source: We view the centromeric chromatin as a mechanical medium that is capable of sustaining biochemical reactions via a spatially non-uniform distribution of Aurora B kinase.

claim: Activity of Aurora B kinase in different chromatin areas depends on both the local concentration of chromatin-tethered Aurora B molecules and on the activity of the soluble Aurora B pool.
source: Activity of this kinase in different chromatin areas depends on both the local concentration of chromatin-tethered Aurora B molecules and on the activity of the soluble Aurora B pool.

claim: The level of Aurora B activity in each local area depends on Aurora B activity in more distant locations of the mechano-biochemical medium.
source: Importantly, our work clearly shows that the level of Aurora B activity in each local area also depends on Aurora B activity in more distant locations of this mechano-biochemical medium.

claim: Activity propagates to more distant areas via phosphorylation in trans by neighboring chromatin-tethered kinase molecules and via their cross-talk with diffusing soluble kinase.
source: This activity then propagates to more distant areas with lower kinase concentration via phosphorylation in trans by neighboring chromatin-tethered kinase molecules and via their cross-talk with diffusing soluble kinase.

claim: A reaction-diffusion system can establish a gradient of kinase activity even if the underlying biochemical pathways are not bistable.
source: Since the concentration of chromatin-bound kinase decreases from the inner centromere to the outer kinetochore, this reaction-diffusion system can establish a gradient of kinase activity even if the underlying biochemical pathways are not bistable (Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 1).

claim: When the bistable coupled kinase-phosphatase system is incorporated into stretchable mechanical matrix, the resulting phosphorylation gradients can be much steeper.
source: However, we demonstrate that when the bistable coupled kinase-phosphatase system is incorporated into this stretchable mechanical matrix, the resulting phosphorylation gradients can be much steeper.

claim: The steep part of the Aurora B activity gradient arises only upon kinetochore stretching and coincides with the outer kinetochore area.
source: Moreover, the steep part of the gradient arises only upon kinetochore stretching and coincides with the outer kinetochore area, where the concentration range for Aurora B kinase causes its bistability.

claim: Steep Aurora B activity gradients are thought to be essential for regulation of kinetochore-microtubule interactions.
source: Thus, bistability affords versatile control of the position and steepness of the resulting gradient, which is thought to be essential for regulation of kinetochore-microtubule interactions (Funabiki and Wynne, 2013; Krenn and Musacchio, 2015).
